newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Caracas stocks slip on local profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: Caracas stocks slip on local profit-taking.

text.p: Caracas stocks slipped for the second day running as local investors took profits even as foreign investors continued to buy into the market, traders said.
"Today's slippage was a natural continuation of yesterday's adjustment," said Financorp broker Hector Perez.
"But there are still interested foreign investors out there buying and you can see that in trade volume," he added.
The market's .IBC index lost 3.82 percent to close at 6,093.39 points as 28 million shares traded worth 6.7 billion bolivars ($14.4 million).
Although stocks fell across the board, traders said market attention was focused on bellwether stock Electricidad de Caracas, which lost 27.45 bolivars to close at 545.55.
"Electricidad was very volatile today," said one broker.
Among traded issues, 31 fell, seven rose and four closed flat -- but traders remained optimistic despite the drop.
"Maybe stocks will fall again tomorrow on another bout of profit-taking. But market sentiment is still good and likely as not there'll probably be rises again at the end of the week," Perez said.
